$comment: The Upskilling Labs home page (src/pages/index.astro): one journey of twenty scenes over a live world, the words beside the picture. The idea it shows: The Labs is one big open project. Everyone in it builds three things together (open workshops and playbooks, the method and kits that turn strangers into teams doing real work, and the platform every Lab runs on), and a small team at the centre curates the official versions every Lab gets. The Build Cycle is the engine: real work, start to finish; when cohorts hit obstacles, Mentors build the next workshops around them; what works is shared back. Everything after the account happens inside it. No levels, pins, membership or dues here.
title: The Upskilling Labs
description: Work is changing too fast to figure out alone. The Upskilling Labs is free workshops and team projects at your local public library, made by volunteers and open to anyone.

title: Find your people.
Build your edge.
hero.orbLabel: The Labs orb at the centre of a living network: local Labs full of people and their projects, orbiting it, with sparks of new ideas travelling between them.
hero.sub: Free workshops and team projects at your local public library, made by volunteers and open to anyone.
hero.$comment: The first screen, after the logo's opening: the hook, then one plain sentence saying what this is. The cycle's dates wait for the scene that explains a Build Cycle. Delivery is local: the programs are most at home at your local public library (DC Public Library is where it started, and the DC Lab's home, not how we deliver everywhere).

model.$comment: The world (src/scripts/orbnet.ts), held on screen through the journey: the camera travels its nineteen scenes as you scroll, and the motif changes shape with them: the system; three of its orbits drawn down into a vortex beneath the orb and wound into one triple helix (the weave); down the helix to each path's own thread, where small scenes play out on it (workshops coming down Learn's thread; strangers becoming a Pod, then teams, a knot freed by a workshop, the Showcase on Build's; contributions rising up Share's to the centre, which sends the official version out to every Lab); the weave again; and the system again, a new Lab born; then close on it, as its first people gather and The Labs' kit reaches it from the centre. Its words: the orb's button, the pause, and what pointing at anything says.

intro.$comment: Written for one person reading it a line at a time, in their order: why this exists, that they're in the right place, who's here, that we'll help (and it grows with what they put in), what it doesn't ask, then the one action.
intro.label: What this is
intro.lede: Work is changing too fast to figure out alone. So we don't.
intro.title: Whoever you are, you're in the right place.
intro.who: Changing careers, just starting out, or decades in and ready to pass it on. We'll help you find your footing, and what you get out of it grows with what you put in.
intro.terms: No tech background needed, and nothing to buy.
intro.note: It's free, and you sign in with Google. Then you'll see what's on near you.

threads.$comment: The three ways in, said plainly (no 'it' to explain). In the world (src/scripts/orbnet.ts) the paths are three of the system's own orbits drawn down into one triple helix. `then` is what each way in says at the close.
threads.title: Learn. Build. Share.
threads.lede: Come to a free workshop. Team up on a twelve-week project. Teach what you know. Start with whichever fits. Most people end up doing all three.
threads.alt: Three of the orb's orbits drawn down into one triple helix: teal, red and gold.

chapters.$comment: The three paths' opening scenes: the world's weave draws in to that path's thread, and its name is set large beside it. Each path's further scenes are in journey.

learn.title: Get sharp, in good company.
learn.lede: Free workshops at your local public library, and some online, on the skills that matter at work right now. No application, no experience needed. Anyone can come.

build.title: Make something real.
build.lede: A Build Cycle is twelve weeks where strangers pick a problem worth solving, team up, and make something that helps.

share.note: How contributing works, and where to start.

share.title: Share what you know.
share.lede: Whatever you add has your name on it.

ways.title: Lead a workshop
ways.body: Or help at one, with whatever you know.

journey.$comment: The journey's scenes between the intro and the close, in order. Each is one idea, shown by the world and said beside it in a line or two.

open.$comment: Where it started, then what we believe and why being early matters. (The open project itself is told at the centre, once the reader has seen what it's made of.)
open.title: It started at the library.
open.lede: In fall 2025, fifty former federal workers met at DC Public Library to work out their next move together. What they started is now open to everyone.
open.belief: We believe what comes next should be shaped by many people, not a few, and that this can become part of how that happens for decades to come. It's early, and the people here now get to decide what it becomes.

workshops.title: Hands-on, with people at every level.

topics.title: Skills that last
topics.body: Communicating, telling a story, framing a problem well.

topics.title: Using AI well
topics.body: What the tools can and can't do, getting good answers, and building simple apps and agents.

photo.alt: A Labs evening at the library: people talking in small groups around the tables.
photo.caption: Pull up a chair: it happens in person, at the library, with people figuring it out alongside you.

pod.title: Strangers become a Pod.
pod.lede: Everyone joins a group of nine or more, called a Pod, around a problem situation you choose together: a real, messy problem people face. It can feel uncertain at first. That's normal, and everyone finds a Pod.

teams.title: Then you find your team.
teams.lede: As ideas take shape, teams of three to five form around the ones people want to make. Mentors, experienced volunteers who've done this before, are there to help. The busiest weeks are at the start and the end.

stuck.title: Every obstacle becomes a workshop.
stuck.lede: When your team hits a wall, a Mentor helps you over it. Then they turn it into a workshop, so the next team doesn't hit the same one.

showcase.title: Show what you made.
showcase.lede: At the end, every team shows its project in public, at the Showcase. Anyone can use what you made, and your name stays on it.

quotes.quote: The program gave me purpose again—connecting me with mission-driven public servants to tackle real problems.
quotes.name: Hector Perla

quotes.quote: I left realizing my gap is exactly where my strength lies—translating between tools, teams, and user needs.
quotes.name: Suzie Zhang

items.title: No lectures.
items.body: Workshops teach skills; your Pod is where you practise.

items.title: Not job placement.
items.body: You leave with something you made, with your name on it, and people who've built with you.

items.title: In person.
items.body: Evenings at your local public library, with some sessions online.

items.title: A real commitment.
items.body: Twelve weeks, busiest at the start and the end.

centre.title: One big open project.
centre.lede: The workshops, the guides, the way a Build Cycle runs, the tools: volunteers make all of it, in the open, and it's free for anyone. Anyone can add to it. What works best in practice is what we keep and share with Labs in other cities, with your name still on it.

together.$comment: The weave again, after the three threads: the loop, then the system.
together.title: It keeps getting better.
together.lede: Every workshop helps a team. Every team's trouble becomes a workshop. Each cycle starts a little further ahead than the last.

labs.title: It starts in your city.
labs.lede: Each city has its own Lab, run by the people in it and at home in its public library. DC is up and running, and we're opening in more cities now.

found.$comment: For people who'd start a Lab where they live, wherever that is (on the list of cities or not). The world closes in on the newborn Lab: a few people gather at it, then The Labs' own kit reaches it from the centre, in silver (the national org). Said a line at a time: you could do this; you don't need experience; what you bring and what we bring; why now; then the account (path=start-a-lab), where founding goes on.
found.title: The next Lab could be yours.
found.lede: Every Lab starts with a few people who want one where they live. You don't need to have done this before.
found.offer: You bring the people. We'll bring the workshops, the Build Cycle and the tools, and help you find it a home at your public library.
found.early: The first people in a city decide what its Lab becomes.
found.note: Make your free account and tell us where you are. We'll talk it through with you.

join.title: Start this week.
join.lede: Come to a workshop, apply for the fall, or tell us what you could teach. Bring what you've got, and we'll help with the rest.
join.note: It's free, and you sign in with Google. We'll show you what's on near you.
join.early: You'd be one of the first.
